messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: rexpokit improvements
parts:
Hi BioGeoBEARS google group,

As you know, the thing that really slows down BioGeoBEARS
(and Lagrange) is the fact that to calculate likelihoods, a
matrix exponentiation has to be performed on every branch of
the tree, and this has to be repeated for all branches for
each step of an ML or Bayesian parameter search.

Matrix exponentiation is fast for small matrices (e.g. 4
areas, 2^4 = 16 states/geographic ranges) but is slow for
large matrices (e.g. 9 areas = 512 states/geographic ranges).

This is a fundamental computational issue and not easily
solved, but computer geniuses can improve the speed somewhat.

For a High-Performance Computing workshop that NIMBioS is
hosting in a few weeks, Drew Schmidt (at the National
Institute for Computational Sciences here at UT Knoxville)
and I got talking about the matrix-exponentiation issue.
Drew knows way more about this than me, and has done some
testing and streamlining of rexpokit, and this results in
some speed improvements. The improvement depends on the
size of the matrix, but it might be something like 40%
improvement for a large matrix.

So, if you would like to try it out, you can get it from
github with:


IMPORTANT NOTES

- Basically this is beta testing at the moment. If it
doesn't work for you, go back to the old rexpokit.

- This is source code, not a binary. Compilation from source
might not work for Windows, or might depend on your compiler
setup.

- Please post the installation output to the group,
especially if you get errors or warnings. These will help
us improve the makefile etc. for the compilation.

- If you notice weird results or crashes, post those to the
group. I anticipate, however, that virtually all problems
people have will be the usual BioGeoBEARS issues (file
formats, too many ranges, and apparent underflow errors
causing NAs during optim/optimx), rather than having
anything to do with rexpokit.

Cheers!
Thanks,
Nick
